issues: The UI primary flow check fails: the test cannot locate and fill the "Email address" field on the Sign‑Up screen. The flow uses a "fill field \"Email address\"" step, which relies on the input being reachable by its label (e.g., via a <label> element, aria‑label, or placeholder). In the current React Native implementation the email input is a TextInput preceded by a <Text> label, which does not create an associated <label> element in the web export, and Playwright’s getByLabel cannot match it. This prevents the acceptance UI flow from completing the sign‑up sequence.

Fix: make the email (and password) inputs discoverable by label on the web build. Options include adding an explicit HTML <label> element (e.g., using a custom component that renders <label> with htmlFor linking to the TextInput’s nativeID), or ensuring the TextInput has a proper aria-label/name that Playwright can match. Using the nativeID prop on TextInput and a <Text> with accessibilityRole='label' and htmlFor may solve the issue. Also verify the placeholder attribute is correctly output. After adjusting the SignUpScreen (and similarly SignInScreen if needed) to provide a proper label association, re‑run the UI flow check – it should pass.
Once the UI flow passes, the static validation will be fully green and the solution can be approved.
feedback: All backend acceptance tests pass, but the UI primary flow test fails because the email field on the sign‑up screen isn’t recognized by the automation. Update the sign‑up (and optionally sign‑in) form to expose a standard <label>‑<input> association (or reliable aria‑label) so the fill step works. After fixing the accessibility labeling, re‑run the checks.
